tldr: This paper demonstrates that large-scale transformers trained via supervised learning on 10 million chess games can approximate search-based value estimation without explicit search, achieving grandmaster-level play (Lichess blitz Elo 2895) with non-trivial generalization to novel board states.
contributions: Introduction of ChessBench, a large-scale benchmark dataset of 530M board states from 10M Lichess games annotated with Stockfish 16, providing 15.3B action-value estimates

Training transformers up to 270M parameters to predict action-values via supervised learning, with resulting policies achieving Lichess blitz Elo of 2895 and puzzle solving ability up to Elo 2867 without explicit search
Extensive ablations on model size, dataset size, architecture, prediction targets (action-values, state-values, behavioral cloning), and loss functions
Open sourcing of the ChessBench dataset, model weights, and training/evaluation code
methods: The authors extracted 10 million games from Lichess and annotated all unique board states with Stockfish 16 as the value oracle (50ms per board), computing state-values (win percentages) and action-values for all legal moves. They trained decoder-only transformers with up to 270M parameters (16 layers, 8 heads, embedding dimension 1024) via supervised learning using cross-entropy loss with HL-Gauss label smoothing. Three prediction targets were compared: action-value prediction (predicting Q-values for state-action pairs), state-value prediction (predicting V-values for board states), and behavioral cloning (predicting oracle best actions). Policies were constructed by either selecting the action with maximal predicted action-value, the action leading to the state with worst opponent value, or the highest-probability cloned action.
results: The 270M parameter transformer achieved a tournament Elo of 2299 against other agents and a Lichess blitz Elo of 2895 against humans (grandmaster level), with puzzle accuracy on challenges rated up to Elo 2867. Action accuracy increased with model scale: 9M params (2025 Elo), 136M params (2259 Elo), 270M params (2895 Elo). The largest model achieved 95.4% puzzle accuracy. Stockfish 16 with 50ms time limit (the oracle) achieved 2713 Elo vs bots and 99.8% puzzle accuracy, while Stockfish with 1.5s per board achieved 2935-2940 Elo. Leela Chess Zero with 400 MCTS simulations achieved 2858 tournament Elo. All tested models showed non-trivial generalization to novel board states.
limitations: Perfect distillation of Stockfish's search-based algorithm remains beyond reach, with a persistent performance gap between supervised transformers and search-based engines like Stockfish 16 (2895 vs 2940 Elo) and Leela Chess Zero with MCTS (2858 tournament Elo). 14.7% of the i.i.d. test set boards overlap with training data (mostly early-game states). The FEN-based input is technically non-Markovian since it cannot capture threefold repetition draws without move history. Playing strength dropped when facing bots versus humans on Lichess, potentially due to different player pools.
